A few good questions

Find your
way in.

Start with a goal, an activity and a little curiosity. These answers explain how the proposed challenge works.

Ask the club
Do I need to be a MISTA member or enter Data4Good?
No. Butler students from any major and degree level may participate. MISTA membership and Data4Good registration are optional. Invited guests may also participate. Individual scores can include eligible team achievements.
Can I submit work completed for a class?
Yes, when it meets the same evidence requirements and falls within the eligible dates. Indicate that it was completed for a course. Fall accomplishments completed before the October launch can qualify, beginning August 26, 2026.
What evidence should I keep?
Keep the certificate, issued badge, verification link, final artifact or organizer confirmation. Reviewers must be able to open it. For a team project, include a brief contribution statement and use the same project identifier as your teammates. Remove unnecessary personal or exam-account information.
Can several teammates earn points for one project?
Yes. Each contributing team member can earn the full listed artifact points after providing a contribution statement. Use a shared project identifier. The project, its poster and a separate pitch are different outcomes, each with its own evidence requirements.
Can the same achievement count more than once?
A course and its completion badge count together. Courses shared across tracks count once, and a track certificate adds no extra points. Preparation and a separately passed certification exam may both count. Retakes and reuploading the same certificate or artifact do not earn additional points.
What happens to fall work in the spring?
Scores reset for spring while your achievement record remains. A new live presentation or a substantial project extension can qualify under its own code. The original course, certificate or poster cannot be claimed again. Work completed from December 24 onward belongs to the spring round.
Do I have to pay for an exam to compete?
A paid certification is optional. Courses, badges and analytical work offer other ways to earn points. Free foundational and advanced club skills clinics are proposed, with dates and available skill families still to be confirmed. These demonstrations award club points, not an industry certification.
How do I get DataCamp or other learning access?
Ask the club for the current invitation, eligibility and expiration details. Data4Good participants may use their existing approved competition access. A catalog listing or Data4Good pathway tag does not guarantee free access to every provider or exam. See the Data4Good program (opens in a new tab) for its published opportunities.
How do I earn the Fall 2026 participation badge?
Earn at least 100 approved points from two or more distinct eligible accomplishments during the fall challenge. Points may come from any category, including a single category. A paid certification is optional. Submit evidence for each accomplishment by the fall deadline. Once your achievements are verified, you qualify for the badge, which you can share on your LinkedIn profile. Receiving this badge adds no competition points. See the badge and an example pathway.
Will my certificates or project evidence be public?
Evidence is for private review. The scoreboard uses your chosen name or alias; you may also opt out of public listing without losing participation badge eligibility. Sharing a project or poster publicly requires separate permission.
When will points appear, and can I request a correction?
Points appear after review and the scoreboard refreshes. If information is missing, reviewers will ask for it. Contact the club promptly about corrections or appeals, and follow the final cutoff for your round. See the proposed review and appeal dates.
Scoring, review & participation badge rules

Participation & evidence

  • All Butler students enrolled during the relevant round may participate, regardless of major, degree level or club membership. December graduates remain eligible for the fall participation badge.
  • Invited alumni, faculty and external students may also participate.
  • Coursework is eligible. Identify whether it was required coursework, an optional extension, independent work or part of another program.
  • Submit evidence reviewers can access. Each contributing team member can earn the full listed artifact points, with a shared project identifier and an individual contribution statement.
  • Follow each activity’s AI-assistance rules, disclose material assistance, verify the results and be able to explain your work.

Fair scoring

  • Each round is capped at 150 learning points, 150 skills points and 200 applied points, for a total of 500. Per-activity limits also apply.
  • A course, its completion badge and overlapping track credit are one learning outcome. Choose the eligible bundle or constituent-course route, never both.
  • Preparation and a separately passed exam can both count. Equivalent exams and skills checks in the same skill family and level share a credit group. A fresh higher level can qualify.
  • A project, poster and separate pitch may earn distinct points. The same presentation occurrence cannot earn both pitch and presentation points.
  • Do not reclaim the same achievement in a later semester. A substantial extension or a new presentation can qualify under its own code.
  • Mentoring and workshop/service credit together are capped at 40 points per round. Payment, access, vouchers, exam retakes, officer titles and competition placement earn no extra points.

Artifact review & free skills routes

Projects and posters are reviewed on five criteria, scored 0–2 each: problem and decision clarity, appropriate evidence and analysis, reproducibility or traceability, communication, and limitations or responsible use. Approval requires at least 7/10 and no zero for evidence or traceability. Approved work receives the fixed catalog points.

Foundational and advanced club skills checks are proposed free routes. Clinic dates, skill families, assistance rules and assessment criteria must be announced before they are available. A skills check uses fresh work, not a project already awarded applied points. These checks award club points, not industry certifications.

Review, corrections & appeals

Claims are reviewed for evidence, completion dates, duplicates and limits before points are awarded. Officers cannot approve their own claims. The faculty adviser handles conflicts and appeals. Badge eligibility is confirmed after the required achievements are approved.

Request corrections promptly. Appeals are due within five business days of the decision, subject to the final round cutoff. Proposed fall provisional results: January 15, 2027; appeal cutoff: January 20; final results: January 22. Proposed spring provisional results: April 21; appeal cutoff: April 23; recognition target: April 26. Final deadline times will be published before launch.

Fall participation badge

Earn the Fall 2026 MISTA-INFORMS Challenge participation badge by accumulating at least 100 approved points from two or more distinct eligible accomplishments during the fall challenge. Points can come from any category, including a single category. A paid certification is optional.

Only verified, nonduplicated achievements within the fall eligibility window count, subject to the published activity and category limits. Team members provide an individual contribution statement. Submit evidence by the fall claim deadline. Badge eligibility does not depend on your leaderboard position. Earning this badge adds no points to your score.

Privacy & your achievement record

Evidence is for private review. Do not include addresses, exam account details or other unnecessary personal information. Public standings use your chosen name or alias; you may opt out of public listing without losing participation badge eligibility. Public sharing of a project or poster requires separate permission.

Scores reset for spring while the achievement record remains. Challenge points express participation incentives and are not a validated measure of ability.
